decisions.quote:
Recently, significant linkage has been
reported to a 39.5 cM region on the long arm of chromosome 2 (2q36-37; PARK11) in North American
Parkinson families under an autosomal dominant model of inheritance. We have performed a replication
study to confirm linkage to this region in a European population. Linkage analysis in 153 individuals from
45 European families with a strong family history of PD did not show any significant LOD score in this
region. Therefore, PARK11 does not seem to play a major role for familial PD in the European population.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped row and the blind coding classify this study as a replication. Prestel et al. (2005) genotyped a new sample of 153 individuals from 45 European families with a strong family history of Parkinson disease across the six markers spanning the 39.5 cM chromosome 2q36-37 (PARK11) region to re-test the autosomal dominant linkage finding reported by Pankratz et al. Prior adjudication/state files do not exist for this key.

decisions.location: abstract, p. 193 (see also Introduction p. 194 and Reference 18 p. 196)
decisions.reason: Considering the shipped original and the same-author/year sibling papers by Pankratz et al. (Ref 17: 2002 initial genome screen in 160 families; Ref 18: 2003b Am J Hum Genet 72:1053-1057, DOI 10.1086/374383, reporting significant autosomal dominant linkage to the 39.5 cM 2q36-37 PARK11 region in 65 families with a strong family history of PD; Ref 19: 2003a Hum Mol Genet 12:2599-2608, confirming 2q36-37 linkage in an expanded sample of 85 families and 362 multiplex families), both the shipped row (paired_target_index 0) and blind target 0 identify Pankratz et al. (2003b, Ref 18, DOI 10.1086/374383) as the primary target whose 39.5 cM autosomal dominant 2q36-37 linkage model, family-history inclusion criteria, and six markers between D2S126 and D2S125 were directly replicated. Prior adjudication/state files do not exist for this key.

decisions.quote:
Recently, significant linkage has been
reported to a 39.5 cM region on the long arm of chromosome 2 (2q36-37; PARK11) in North American
Parkinson families under an autosomal dominant model of inheritance. We have performed a replication
study to confirm linkage to this region in a European population. Linkage analysis in 153 individuals from

decisions.reason: Both the shipped row and the blind coding agree that the replication outcome is failed. Prestel et al. (2005) state an explicit overall verdict that linkage analysis in 153 individuals from 45 European families did not show any significant LOD score in the 2q36-37 region, and every tested analysis (multipoint parametric and nonparametric linkage in all 45 families, repeat linkage analysis in 36 families after excluding 9 families with possible linkage to parkin marker D6S305, and S-TDT allele transmission tests) failed to confirm linkage to PARK11. Prior adjudication/state files do not exist for this key.
